hook_text: A turtle lays about a hundred eggs, then swims away forever. Only one or two in a thousand make it.
clip_script: Night on an iSimangaliso beach. A leatherback turtle digs a nest, lays her eggs and slips back into the sea. She will never meet her babies. Two months later, the hatchlings dash for the waves. Crabs, birds and fish are waiting. Death can happen at any stage. That is why turtles lay so many eggs. Now a crocodile mother: she guards her nest and carries her babies to the water in her mouth. Few young, lots of care.
visual_style: Whiteboard beach at night with a turtle nest, tiny hatchlings racing to the sea, then a crocodile carrying babies.
mood: Gentle and moving, like a nature documentary at night.
pacing: Slow nest scene, fast hatchling dash, then a warm finish with the crocodile mother.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare how three animals care for their young.
